sources.title: Stephen Gould, Basura Fernando, Anoop Cherian, Peter Anderson, Rodrigo Santa Cruz, and Edison Guo, On Differentiating Parameterized Argmin and Argmax Problems with Application to Bi-level Optimization
sources.locator: Complete 16-page report; §3.1–3.2, Lemmas 3.1–3.3, PDF pp. 3–4, for stationary-point derivatives, the vector formula, and multiple parameter directions; §3.2, PDF pp. 4–5, for multiple stationary branches and selection caveats. Lemma 3.2's displayed assumptions do not explicitly state Hessian nonsingularity or a differentiable local branch; those hypotheses are supplied and proved locally through the Euclidean implicit-function theorem.

contents.name: The parameterized lower-level/upper-level objective setup and the distinction between a selected stationary branch and a global optimizer
The vector stationary-point derivative -H^{-1}B and its multiple-parameter extension
Multiple stationary points require consistent branch selection; the paper's derivative argument is used only with the local nonsingularity hypotheses proved from the IFT here

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.S096, Matrix Calculus for Machine Learning and Beyond, Lecture 4 Part 2: Nonlinear Root-Finding, Optimization, and Adjoint-Method Differentiation
sources.locator: Complete 9-page lecture note read; §6.3.1–6.3.2, PDF pp. 6–7 (printed pp. 43–44), for the implicit nonlinear-system derivative, transposed adjoint equation, and the distinction from differentiating an approximate finite solve.

contents.name: Differentiate a scalar objective through a locally defined nonsingular nonlinear residual and move the derivative to one transposed linear adjoint solve
The implicit residual derivative route and exact local branch convention
Finite iterative solves and their stopped derivatives are separate from the exact implicit derivative

sources.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis II, §8.5.1, Theorem 8.5.6: Implicit Function Theorem
sources.locator: Complete relevant section read: §8.5.1, Theorem 8.5.6 and proof. The proof constructs F(x,y)=(x,f(x,y)), proves its derivative invertible from the block derivative, applies the inverse-function theorem, extracts the unique local branch, and differentiates the zero identity for the derivative formula.

contents.name: A C1 residual with an invertible state-block Jacobian has a locally unique C1 solution branch with derivative -A_y^{-1}A_x
